title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Mathematics - Conic Sections (Parabola)
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let the parabola $y = x^2 + px + q$ passing through the point $(1, -1)$ be such that the distance between its vertex and the $x$-axis is minimum. Then the value of $p^2 + q^2$ is:
questions.explain:
Since the parabola passes through $(1,-1)$, we have $-1 = 1 + p + q \implies q = -2 - p$.
The vertex of the parabola is at $(-\frac{p}{2}, -\frac{p^2}{4} + q)$. The distance to the $x$-axis is $|-\frac{p^2}{4} + q| = |-\frac{p^2}{4} - p - 2| = \frac{1}{4}|p^2 + 4p + 8|$.
To minimize $\frac{1}{4}((p+2)^2 + 4)$, we set $p = -2$. 
Then $q = -2 - (-2) = 0$.
The value of $p^2 + q^2 = (-2)^2 + 0^2 = 4$.
